pr_body:
ColumnDescriptor.ColID() was not updated to use LogicalColumnID
so the ordinal position of a column could be incorrect in some cases.

No release note since bug is not in production.

Release note: None

Fixes #52305
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/52309)
Test was flaking because I think in newOptTable(), one of the ColID calls should actually be referring to the PhysicalColumnID and not LogicalColumnID

> I don't understand - why are we adding a cat API that isn't used? (outside of the internal implementation)

Do you mean PhysicalColID? It's used in newOptTable.

I added it because previously we had ColID which referred to both the LogicalColumnID and PhysicalColumnID due to the fact that we had no concept of LogicalColumnID (it was introduced to support ALTER COLUMN TYPE).

However I think in newOptTable(), colMap should actually refer to the physical ColumnID (correct me if I'm wrong).
@RichardJCai I'm not following what's going on here. I thought the logical column ID should only be accessed by catalog tables? The optimizer should be just dealing with the column's `ID`.

> In plan_opt.go in the prepareUsingOptimizer function, we use ColID() to get the stable id of the column, however this changes after ALTER COLUMN TYPE when ColID refers to the physical ColumnID, this one should be the LogicalColumnID.

This case is just for displaying information as part of a pgwire header. This can use the logical column ID. However, you don't need to add to the `cat.Column` interface -- just asserting it into a column desc and getting the necessary information is fine.

> For resolveNumericColumnRefs in util.go ColID is mapped to an ordinal as well.
In this case, after an ALTER COLUMN TYPE, we want the ordinal to stay the same for the column that is altered, however ColID is bumped and the ordinal changes even though it shouldn't. That's the case I added to the logictest in this PR. I'm gonna try to cleanup these cases for this PR. Some of the assumptions about the ColumnID that we had are not true anymore due to ALTER COLUMN TYPE.

This function looks up columns by their ID in the table. It definitely should be using the column's actual ID. It will be up to alter column type to change column ID references if they are ever serialized.

> > For resolveNumericColumnRefs in util.go ColID is mapped to an ordinal as well.
> > In this case, after an ALTER COLUMN TYPE, we want the ordinal to stay the same for the column that is altered, however ColID is bumped and the ordinal changes even though it shouldn't. That's the case I added to the logictest in this PR. I'm gonna try to cleanup these cases for this PR. Some of the assumptions about the ColumnID that we had are not true anymore due to ALTER COLUMN TYPE.
> 
> This function looks up columns by their ID in the table. It definitely should be using the column's actual ID. It will be up to alter column type to change column ID references if they are ever serialized.

You're right this should just be ID, we have this edge case for ALTER COLUMN ID, I'll open a separate issue for this.

I think this current issue is just a matter of making some documentation clearer and fixing the PGAttributeNum case.

Closing this for now. Seems like in this case, we actually want to use ID, not LogicalColumnID. 
Will open a PR adding some comments to make it clear.

There is a separate issue regarding numeric column references after an alter column type.
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/52305

Agreed, it really should be ColumnID
We should not have two different, subtly-different column ID's in this interface. This will cause subtle bugs for years down the road as developers pick the wrong one to use in any given situation. I think we need to go back to the drawing board, since this indicates that something may be wrong architecturally deeper down, perhaps with how ALTER COLUMN TYPE is working.

issue_context.title: sql: alter column type changes numeric id of column
issue_context.body:
Example:

Alter column type changes the id.

Here's an example where the behaviour is shown - after alter column type, the column should have the same ordinal, however since it ColID refers to ID instead of LogicalColumnID, the column cannot be found after the alter column type.

This is not necessarily an "error" since we defined the syntax to refer to the ColumnID, although maybe it should refer to the LogicalColumnID?

```
root@127.0.0.1:52410/movr> SET enable_experimental_alter_column_type_general = true;
SET

Time: 241µs

root@127.0.0.1:52410/movr> alter table t alter column x type string;
root@127.0.0.1:52410/movr> create table t(x int);
CREATE TABLE

Time: 2.663ms

root@127.0.0.1:52410/movr> select * from [59(1) as t];
  x
-----
(0 rows)

Time: 2.873ms

root@127.0.0.1:52410/movr> alter table t alter column x type string;
NOTICE: ALTER COLUMN TYPE changes are finalized asynchronously; further schema changes on this table may be restricted until the job completes; some writes to the altered column may be rejected until the schema change is finalized
ALTER TABLE

Time: 92.198ms

root@127.0.0.1:52410/movr> select * from [59(1) as t];
ERROR: column [1] does not exist
SQLSTATE: 42703
root@127.0.0.1:52410/movr>
root@127.0.0.1:52410/movr> select * from [59(2) as t];
--
(0 rows)

Time: 542µs
```

Code here should be 
```
// ColID is part of the cat.Column interface.
func (desc *ColumnDescriptor) ColID() cat.StableID {
	return cat.StableID(desc.ID)
}
```
comments: Closing since this isn't exactly a bug.

review_comments: What error happens if this isn't here? I'm very dubious about this line.

This logic test fails for ALTER COLUMN TYPE with `requested column y not in index`

Alter column type creates a new column with the new type and "swaps" it with the original column. There's a state where we set the LogicalColumnID of the new column to the LogicalColumnID of the original column (which in this test case happens to be the physical ColumnID as well). However the original column is dropped and there is no more column with the column of the original physical ColumnID, I think this mapping maps columns to their physical column id so when it looks up using the LogicalColumnID (which is the original columns physical ColumnID) there is no column. Correct me if I'm wrong or if this explanation is too confusing.

From what I understand, colMap should actually map the physical ColumnID of the column to the ordinal.

```	
// colMap is a mapping from unique ColumnID to column ordinal within the
	
// table. This is a common lookup that needs to be fast.
	
colMap map[sqlbase.ColumnID]int
``` 

```
statement ok
ALTER TABLE t13 ALTER COLUMN y TYPE STRING

query IT
SELECT x, y FROM t13 ORDER BY x
----
1  1
2  2
```
@RaduBerinde can you comment on this? I don't know enough.
